messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SE1 region alert — elevated 5xx (inference-backend) detected. P95 latency spike and connection errors to model servers. Pager: @josh_oncall, @anna_ops. Auto-reroute policy may trigger if errors persist.

josh_oncall: on it, looking at metrics and router logs. any customer reports?

maria_support: we have two customers flagged by monitoring with increased errors (acct: acme-inc, acct: fontapp). No external tickets yet, CS alerted.

anna_ops: quick summary — southeast1 (se1) started seeing connection resets from the inference pool ~03:42 UTC. KV-cache warming still working but model RPCs failing 502/504.

lee_sre: I'm pulling scheduler and LB stats now. If this is egress or infra, we should announce an internal mitigation and start status update.

sam_platform: I see a flurry of ssh errors from the edge NATs in se1 around 03:40. Routing to egress peers transiently failing. Suspect peering flap that affects our model-serving control plane.

josh_oncall: confirmed 5xx spike in hosted-api->model-serving graph. Starting temporary traffic diversion to us-central1 for critical tenants. Will keep non-critical traffic on degraded se1 to reduce cascading.

anna_ops: action items: 1) start diversion policy for customer-tier "prod-critical" to fallback region 2) post status page draft 3) prepare customer-facing blurb. I'll handle 1 and 2.

anna_ops: applying diversion policy now:

```
# temporary routing rule
route.apply --from-region=se1 --to-region=us-central1 --filter=customer_tier:prod-critical --dry-run=false
```

deploy-bot: rollout started for route.apply (id: r-1981-se1-failover). Expect ~15s to propagate.

josh_oncall: propagation noted. telemetry shows error rates for prod-critical dropping in se1 and rising in us-central1 — that matches diversion.

patrick_product: do we have a short status page entry? we should mention degraded performance and partial reroute.

anna_ops: drafting status page (short form) — please review: 

"We are investigating elevated error rates for hosted inference in the southeast1 region. We have enabled temporary regional routing to move critical customer traffic to an alternative region to reduce impact. Users in SE1 may see increased latency or errors while we stabilize. Root cause under investigation."

patrick_product: 👍 add ETA for next update in 30 minutes and note customers can expect occasional 502s.

anna_ops: updated: 

"Update (30m): We have enabled temporary routing for critical customers to us-central1 which has reduced errors for those tenants. Engineers are investigating network peering between our SE1 edge and upstream provider. Non-critical traffic may still experience errors or increased latency. Next update in 30 minutes or on significant change."

maria_support: customer message draft for CS/Email — please edit: 

"Hi <customer>,
We detected elevated errors for requests served from our southeast1 region starting at ~03:40 UTC which may cause intermittent 502/504 errors or higher latency. We’ve routed critical traffic to another region to reduce impact. No data breach or model integrity issue. We’ll provide updates in our status page and are available via your support contact for questions. Apologies for the disruption. — Redwood Inference Ops"

patrick_product: add note about possible increased cost for routed requests since they cross regions. good to flag.

maria_support: edited and ready to send for impacted accounts (acme-inc, fontapp).

lee_sre: quick mitigation checklist for docs/internal comms (for CS and AMs):
- Incident summary and timeline (include start ts)
- Regions affected: southeast1 primary, with potential latency cross-impact in nearby edge pops
- Action taken: temporary routing for prod-critical -> us-central1, monitoring enabled
- Suggested customer guidance: retry/backoff, specify region pinning if needed
- Escalation contacts: SRE, Platform, Product

sam_platform: I'm opening a ticket with our peering provider (ticket #PP-8942) and attaching traceroutes and NAT logs. Also spinning up a small extra instance group in se1 to try to absorb load while upstream is validated.

josh_oncall: can we add a fallback model variant (smaller quantized) for non-critical to reduce load? that could help.

lee_sre: yes — adding a temporary route that switches model variant for non-critical traffic:

```
policy.update --region=se1 --target=noncritical --model-variant=llama2-mini-q4 --duration=60m
```

deploy-bot: policy.update applied (policy id: p-1981-variant).

maria_support: sending customer emails now to acme-inc and fontapp with the edited text. tagging CS leads.

patrick_product: drafting public status page post for external customers based on the internal update. we'll use central status:redwood-status.io/incidents/1981.

anna_ops: internal comms template for AMs (copyable):

"Hi <AM>,
Quick heads up: we experienced elevated inference errors in SE1 starting at <03:40 UTC>. We've routed critical customers to another region and applied temporary model-variant degradation for non-critical workloads to reduce pressure. Impact: potential 502s and increased latency for some users in SE1. Root cause appears related to upstream peering instability; we are coordinating with the provider. We will update you at <+30m> and when normal routing is restored. Contact oncall or SRE for urgent escalations.
Regards, Ops"

josh_oncall: logging timeline and actions in the incident tracker (incident-1981). Will add links to reroute policy and provider ticket.

lee_sre: latest diag: NAT timeouts and BGP flap between our se1 edge and provider ntt-sea-agg. Provider acknowledges and is investigating. Next: confirmation of BGP stability or further mitigation (e.g., alternate peer).

sam_platform: preparing to failover at the egress peer level if provider doesn't stabilize in 15m. will coordinate with netops.

anna_ops: next update for status page in 20m. If provider confirms fix, we'll start draining diverted traffic back and post recovery notes.

patrick_product: FYI for docs — add a short FAQ line: "Why did my requests route to another region?" -> "We applied a temporary routing policy to protect critical traffic while we remediate a regional networking issue. Responses may come from another region and could be slightly slower or incur cross-region cost."

maria_support: CS thread created and assigned to support lead @sarah_cs (not in this thread).

deploy-bot: route r-1981-se1-failover status: propagated to 98% of edge nodes; 2% pending.

josh_oncall: handoff plan — I'll stay for the next 25m and then hand to @anna_ops for monitoring while I sleep. If still open at +60m, escalate to oncall2.

anna_ops: acknowledged, will take the next watch. Preparing final copy for public status now.

incident-bot: NOTE: add runbook snapshot link to incident-1981: https://redwood-internal/infra/incidents/1981/runbook-snapshot.

lee_sre: small reminder for postmortem: capture the decision to apply regional routing and the timing, and estimate customer exposure and any extra cross-region charges applied to customers.

maria_support: closing loop: customer emails delivered. I'll surface any replies here.

josh_oncall: update 09:15 UTC — provider reports BGP updates stabilized, errors trending down in se1. beginning gradual rollback of routing policy (will proceed cautiously).

anna_ops: rollback command: 

```
route.rollback --id=r-1981-se1-failover --step=gradual --monitor=errors,latency --threshold=2%errors
```

deploy-bot: rollback started, monitoring enabled.

josh_oncall: errors back to baseline. closing incident and scheduling postmortem. thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:

patrick_product: please add short recovery blurb to status: "Service recovered in SE1. Temporary reroutes removed. Investigating with peering provider — postmortem to follow."

anna_ops: posted recovery and created postmortem ticket (PM-1981). Handoff complete to @anna_ops for write-up.

maria_support: marking CS action items done; will summarize customer impact in the postmortem.

incident-bot: Incident 1981234567 CLOSED by josh_oncall (duration ~35m).
